name: OpenWebUI
what: A chat front end for local and remote models with users, tools and a document store. It holds people's conversations, which is why the dashboard looks at it only from outside.
licence: BSD-3-Clause with a branding clause (read upstream's LICENSE)

drivers.schtasks: three Windows scheduled tasks owui-ctl-start/stop/update exist
drivers.systemd: a systemd unit serves it: three owui-ctl-* control units for a system unit (contrib/openwebui-systemd), or its own user unit
drivers.docker-compose: a container from ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui publishes the port and carries Compose labels (com.docker.compose.project, .service): setup writes the project, files, service and named volumes from them
drivers.docker: a container started with docker run: seen, but the tile drives Compose projects only
drivers.pip: the open-webui package is installed in a venv

can: start, stop and update it through its driver
show health, version and the tail of its control logs
cannot: read its data: conversations, users, settings and the database are off limits by rule

update.note: The service's own driver updates it: the scheduled task or control unit, which back up as they were written to; the docker-compose driver, which copies the named volumes, pulls, recreates and rolls image and data back if the new version does not come up; or pip install -U open-webui by hand. Upstream's release notes say when a version migrates the database.

docker: In a folder of its own, a docker-compose.yml with one service: image ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main, ports "127.0.0.1:3000:8080", volumes open-webui:/app/backend/data (a named volume, which is what an update copies), extra_hosts host.docker.internal:host-gateway so it can reach engines on the host, restart unless-stopped.
docker compose up -d in that folder. A plain docker run works too, but the tile drives Compose projects only.
pip: python -m venv owui && owui/Scripts/pip install open-webui
then: Open http://127.0.0.1:3000, make the first (admin) account, point Connections at your engines' OpenAI-style endpoints.

good: a front end for several people and several engines
tools, document search and personas on top of local models
not: a dashboard for the machine: that is this
exposure beyond the machine without a reverse proxy and its own login
